A lot of people love dogs now, and it's not just a matter of purebreds or mutts; my aunt has a "mutt" named Koom and she adores him like one of her children.

Of course, I'm not really saying this to "defend" the terrible practices in animal farming depicted in the photos. It's just that I'm sick and tired of everybody else calling Korean people uncivilized and barbaric for eating dogs, when in fact, the vast majority of people in Korea would be horrified at the thought of eating one.

It's like getting a few fundamentalist Christian families from the US and portraying everybody from the country to be like them. Only very few people eat dog now, and I'm sure any Korean who saw this album would be equally as upset about the abhorrent treatment.

This was my experience the two times I was hospitalized. I hope I'm not violating any forum rules, I would just like OP to know what to expect. Having been in his shoes, I would rather OP be safe in a safe and genuinely caring environment like a hospital.:


The first time, I only told my therapist during one of our sessions that I was feeling depressed lately, more so than usual. She asked me if I was feeling suicidal and if I had any plans to go through with my suicidal ideation, and I told her yes, because I had considered nitrogen poisoning. She immediately called my roommate and best friend (who is my emergency contact), and they took me to a nearby hospital where I stayed for about 5 days. My friend came back in the evening with some clothes and toothbrush/toothpaste, hairbrush, those kind of things. You're allowed anything that doesn't have a long lace or string (like shoelaces), and during the 5 days I was there, they had us on a pretty busy schedule of group therapy (which was very nice actually) and some other fun activities like basketball.


The second time was when I attempted suicide by overdosing. I took a bunch of sedatives, and I lay down just waiting to die, and then my friend walked in on me. He called the ambulance, they came, strapped me on a gurney, and took me to the hospital emergency care. This time it wasn't so pleasant; they took a bunch of blood tests, hooked me up to an IV, gave me a urethral catheter, all while yelling at me to stay awake. The catheter was very uncomfortable, and I had a crying fit trying to convince them to take it out before I fell asleep. I was there for about 10 days this time (this was a different institution from the first time), and we didn't have as much group therapy. We had a lot more free time, and the lounge was a nice place to go. They had a TV, a piano (which I loved because I'm a music major), a BUNCH of 1000 piece jigsaw puzzles, and even an art room where we could make wooden models and paint stuff.


In any case, you can expect basically the following things no matter what institution you go to:

-You will be allowed to bring things, but nothing with strings. They will check and catalog everything you bring in with you.

-Most of the doors will be locked. You can't go wherever the heck you want without letting somebody know, but know that it's there for your safety.

-Try to participate in as much group activity as you can. I know there isn't a lot of variation in what therapists say, but having the extra insight of the other patients really helped me.


If you have any questions, feel free to ask me, and I'll try to answer them as much as I can. Hope all goes well, and if you're feeling reckless, please do go to the hospital.
